reassurance: Most people are glad to be asked. It usually goes better than you expect.
The first line matters less than your next question. Ask, then listen.
People usually like you more than you think after a conversation.
Going a little deeper is usually less awkward than people fear.
You don't need a clever line. A real question and real interest are enough.
A short conversation counts. You can leave whenever it feels right.
reassuranceText: Hearing from you out of the blue is appreciated more than people expect.
A short message is enough. It doesn't need to be perfect.

exits.line: I'm going to say hello to a few more people, but I'm glad we talked. Good luck with what you mentioned.
I should let you get back to everyone. I really enjoyed this.
Before I go: what was the name of the thing you recommended? I want to look it up.
I'm going to catch the next session. May I get in touch about what we discussed?
I've really enjoyed this. Shall we swap details before I move on?
I'll let you get to your next thing. Thanks, that was helpful.
Looks like we should get started. I'd like to hear the rest afterwards.
I'll let you go. Good to catch up before the day runs away.
I'd better keep moving, but it was good to bump into you. Enjoy the rest of your day.
I need to get going. It was good to see you.
Looks like they're finishing up. Good talking to you. See you next time.
I'm going to help in the kitchen, but I want to hear the rest of that later.
Thanks for the company. That made the drive go faster.
I'll let you get on with your evening. I'm glad we talked.
I'll let you get on with your day. Talk soon.
No need to reply to this one. Good to hear from you.
Thanks for telling me that. I'm glad I asked.
I like hearing what's on your mind. More later?
No need to reply. See you tonight.
Thanks for telling me. That's all from me.
No need to reply. See you later.
Thank you for telling me. I love hearing about your day.
I've had a really good time. Shall we do this again?
I'll let you go. Looking forward to seeing you.

hardTime.line: It's really good to see you.
I've been thinking about you.
That sounds really hard. I'm sorry you're dealing with it.
hardTime.tip: Say it, then leave room. No need to fill the silence.

hardTime.line: I don't know what to say, but I'm glad I'm here with you.
Do you feel like talking about it, or would a distraction be better?
hardTime.tip: Either answer is fine. Follow their lead.

hardTime.line: What's today been like?
hardTime.tip: Smaller than "How are you?", so it's easier to answer honestly.

hardTime.line: I'd love to hear about them, if you feel like telling me.
hardTime.tip: For a loss. Use the person's name if you know it.

hardTime.line: No need to go into it. I just wanted you to know I noticed.
I'm going to the store tomorrow. What can I pick up for you?
hardTime.tip: A specific offer is easier to accept than "let me know".

hardTime.line: Can I bring dinner over one night this week? You wouldn't have to host me.
hardTime.tip: Name the night if you can.

hardTime.line: I can take something off your list this week. What would help most?
hardTime.tip: Offer one concrete thing if they can't think of any.

hardTime.line: I can cover that for you if it would help. Just say the word.
Thinking of you today. No need to reply.
I heard things have been hard. I'm sorry. No need to reply.
No words needed. I'm here, and I'm not going anywhere.
Would a call help, or would you rather I just keep sending you silly things?
I'm dropping some food at your door tonight. No need to answer it.
I'm free Saturday morning. Can I take something off your hands?
hardTime.tip: Swap in a time you can really do.

hardTime.line: You've had a lot on. I see how much you're carrying.
What would help most tonight: talking it through, or a break from it?
I'll take tomorrow morning. You rest.
Come and sit with me for a minute. We don't have to talk.
Thinking about you today. I'm on your side.
I've got dinner tonight. Don't think about it.
Rough one? Tell me later if you want to. No pressure.
Looks like it was a rough day. I'm around if you want company.
hardTime.tip: Say it once, then leave it. Being nearby is enough.

hardTime.line: I'm making food. Want some?
hardTime.tip: Side by side beats face to face. Don't ask what's wrong.

hardTime.line: You don't have to tell me about it. If you do want to, I'll just listen.
hardTime.tip: Then really just listen. No advice unless asked.

hardTime.line: No need to reply. I love you and I'm here.
Picking up food on my way home. What do you want?
Seemed like a hard day. Here if you want to talk, fine if you don't.
You look like you had a tough day. Do you want a cuddle or some quiet time?
What was the hardest part of today?
hardTime.tip: Try at bedtime, lights low. Listen without solving it.

hardTime.line: Shall we read something together, just you and me?
That sounds like it felt really big. I'm right here.
